explanation:

has only one real root in the interval (0,1)

question: A cone has vertical angle 60°, and its total surface area increases at the rate of 4√3 cm²/sec. The rate of change of its volume when the radius is 4 cm is
explanation:

question: The surface area of a sphere is 64 π sq cm. If it increases by 0.02 sq cm, the approximate increase in its volume (in cc) is
explanation:

Approximate change in volume = (r/2) x change in S = (⁴⁄₂)(0.02) = 0.04

question: If the normal to the curve y²=8x at the point (2,4) meets the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B, then OA+OB (O is the origin) is
explanation:

explanation:

question: The value of the integral from 0 to π/3 of sin2x/(1+cos2x) dx is
explanation:

subject: Maths
question: The value of the integral from -π to π of x² sinx dx is
explanation:
The integrand x² sinx is the product of an even function (x²) and an odd function (sinx), which makes the whole function odd
The integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval [-π,π] is always 0

subject: Maths
question: The area of the region (in square units) bounded by the curve y=x²-9, the x-axis, and the lines x=-3, x=4 is
explanation:
The curve crosses the x-axis at x=-3 and x=3
Between x=-3 and x=3, the curve lies below the axis, contributing an area of 36 (absolute value)
Between x=3 and x=4, the curve lies above the axis, contributing an area of ¹⁰⁄₃
Total area = 36+¹⁰⁄₃ = ¹¹⁸⁄₃

subject: Maths
question: If A and B are arbitrary constants, the differential equation for the family y=A e²ˣ+B e⁻²ˣ is
explanation:
y prime = 2A e²ˣ - 2B e⁻²ˣ
y double-prime = 4A e²ˣ + 4B e⁻²ˣ = 4y

subject: Maths
question: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = (x²+y²)/(2xy) is
explanation:
This is a homogeneous equation, so substitute y=vx
After substitution, the equation reduces to 2v/(1-v²) dv = dx/x
Integrating gives -ln|1-v²| = ln|x| + C, which simplifies to x(1-v²) = constant
Substituting back v=y/x and simplifying gives x²-y² = Cx

subject: Maths
question: The general solution of the differential equation (x+2y+1)dy = (2x+y-1)dx is
explanation:
Shift variables using x=X+1, y=Y-1 to remove the constants, giving the homogeneous equation dY/dX=(2X+Y)/(X+2Y)
Substituting Y=vX and using partial fractions to integrate leads to (1-v)³(1+v) X⁴ = constant
Substituting back v=Y/X and simplifying gives (X-Y)³(X+Y) = C
Finally substituting X=x-1, Y=y+1 gives (x-y-2)³(x+y) = C

subject: Maths
question: If A is a 3×3 matrix with det(A)=5, then det(2A) =
explanation:
For an n x n matrix, det(kA) = kⁿ det(A)

subject: Physics
question: If Q, C, and V represent charge, capacitance, and potential respectively, the physical quantity having the dimensions of QV is
explanation:
The work done in moving a charge Q through a potential difference V is W=QV
So QV has the dimensions of energy

subject: Physics
question: A body falls freely under gravity from rest. The total displacement during the first half-second, third half-second, and fifth half-second of its motion is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
Displacement in interval [t1,t2] is (½)g(t2²-t1²)
First half-second [0,0.5]: (½)(10)(0.25-0)=1.25 m
Third half-second [1.0,1.5]: (½)(10)(2.25-1)=6.25 m
Fifth half-second [2.0,2.5]: (½)(10)(6.25-4)=11.25 m
Total = 1.25+6.25+11.25 = 18.75 m

subject: Physics
question: The minimum velocity of a projectile during its motion is 20 m/s, and the ratio of its vertical to horizontal displacement at t=2s is 1:2. The angle of projection is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
The minimum speed during projectile motion occurs at the top and equals the horizontal component, so ux=20 m/s
Horizontal displacement at t=2: x=20(2)=40 m
Ratio y:x=1:2 gives vertical displacement y=20 m
y=uy(2)-(½)(10)(4)=2uy-20=20, so uy=20 m/s
Initial speed u=√(400+400)=20√2 m/s
tan(θ)=uy/ux=²⁰⁄₂₀=1, so θ=45°

subject: Physics
question: A body is projected at 40 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. The time taken for the velocity vector to become perpendicular to the initial velocity vector is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
Using the standard result, the time for the velocity to become perpendicular to the initial velocity is t=u/(g sin(θ))
With u=40, θ=30°, g=10: t=40/(10 x 0.5)=⁴⁰⁄₅=8 s

subject: Physics
question: A small bead is placed on a circular loop of radius 20 cm rotating about its vertical diameter with angular velocity 10 rad/s. The angle made by the radius vector to the bead with the vertical downward direction is (g=10 m/s², neglect friction)
explanation:
For a bead on a rotating vertical circular wire, cos(θ) = g/(ω² r)
g=10, ω=10, r=0.2 m
ω² r = 100(0.2) = 20
cos(θ) = ¹⁰⁄₂₀ = 0.5
θ = cos⁻¹(0.5)

subject: Physics
question: A body placed at the top of an inclined plane of angle tan⁻¹(⁴⁄₃) takes time T to reach the bottom when the plane is smooth, and time 2T when rough. The coefficient of kinetic friction is
explanation:
On the smooth incline, a1 = g sin(θ); on the rough incline, a2 = g[sin(θ)-μ cos(θ)]
Since the same distance is covered, a1=4a2 (because time is doubled)
sin(θ) = 4[sin(θ)-μ cos(θ)]
4 μ cos(θ) = 3 sin(θ)
μ = (¾)tan(θ) = (¾)(⁴⁄₃) = 1

subject: Physics
question: An 8 kg block is pushed by a force of 150 N over a distance of 8 m on a surface with coefficient of friction 0.25. The final kinetic energy of the block is (g=10 m/s²)
explanation:
Friction force = 0.25 x 8 x 10 = 20 N
Net force = 150-20 = 130 N
Work done by the net force = 130 x 8 = 1040 J, which equals the final kinetic energy since the block starts from rest

subject: Physics
question: A force F=6x² is applied to move an object from x=0 to x=3 m. The work done is
explanation:
Work done = the ∫Fdx from 0 to 3
= the ∫6x²dx from 0 to 3
= 2x³ evaluated from 0 to 3
= 2(27) = 54 J

subject: Physics
question: A thin wire of length L and mass m is bent into a square loop. The moment of inertia of the loop about an axis through its center perpendicular to its plane is
explanation:
The square has side a=L/4
By calculating the moment of inertia of each side about the perpendicular axis through the center and summing over all four sides (using symmetry), the total works out to ma²/3
Substituting a=L/4 gives mL²/48

subject: Physics
question: A ball moves in a horizontal circle with initial speed v0 and radius R on a surface with friction coefficient μ. The distance travelled by the ball before it comes to rest is
explanation:
Friction provides a constant tangential deceleration a = μ g
Using v²=v0²-2as with final velocity 0
s = v0²/(2 μ g)

subject: Physics
question: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with time period T and amplitude A, starting from rest. The distance travelled in time T/8 is
explanation:
Since the particle starts from rest at the extreme position, x(t)=A cos(ω t), ω=2π/T
At t=T/8, ω t = π/4
x = A cos(π/4) = A/√2
Distance travelled = A - A/√2 = A(2-√2)/2 (after rationalizing)

subject: Physics
question: Two blocks of masses m and 3m connected by a spring of constant K are given velocities V in opposite directions towards each other. The maximum compression of the spring is
explanation:
The reduced mass is μ = m(3m)/(m+3m) = 3m/4
Relative velocity of approach = 2V
Kinetic energy in relative motion = (½)(3m/4)(2V)² = 3mV²/2
At maximum compression, this equals the spring energy: (½)Kx² = 3mV²/2
x = V √(3m/K)

subject: Physics
question: The work required to shift an artificial satellite from an orbit of radius r to an orbit of radius 3r is
explanation:
Total energy in a circular orbit of radius r is E=-GMm/(2r)
Work done = E(3r)-E(r) = -GMm/(6r)-(-GMm/(2r)) = GMm[-⅙+½] = GMm(⅓)/r = GMm/(3r)

subject: Physics
question: A material has a linear stress-strain graph with stress=80 N/m² at strain=4×10⁻³. The elastic energy density at a strain of 3×10⁻³ is
explanation:
Young modulus Y = stress/strain = 80/(4×10⁻³) = 2×10⁴ N/m²
At strain 3×10⁻³, stress = Y x strain = 2×10⁴ x 3×10⁻³ = 60 N/m²
Energy density = (½) x stress x strain = (½)(60)(3×10⁻³) = 0.09 J/m³ = 9×10⁻² J/m³

subject: Physics
question: A large tank is filled with water to height h and drains through a small hole at the bottom. The ratio of the time taken for the level to fall from h to h/3, to the time taken to fall from h/3 to zero, is
explanation:
Time to drain from h1 to h2 is ∝ √(h1)-√(h2)
Time for h to h/3 is ∝ √(h)-√(h/3) = √(h)[1-1/√3]
Time for h/3 to 0 is ∝ √(h/3) = √(h)/√3
Ratio = √3[1-1/√3] = √3-1

question: Three identical rods A, B, C meet at a common junction. The free end of A is at 0° Celsius, the free end of B is at 60° Celsius, and the free end of C is at 90° Celsius. The junction temperature is
explanation:
At steady state, heat flowing in from B and C equals heat flowing out through A
(60-T)/R + (90-T)/R = (T-0)/R
150-2T = T
150 = 3T
T = 50° C

subject: Physics
question: Two gases A and B start at the same pressure, volume, and temperature. A is compressed isothermally and B adiabatically, both to one-third the initial volume. The final pressure of A compared to B is
explanation:
Final pressure of A (isothermal): Pₐ = 3P0
Final pressure of B (adiabatic): PB = P0 . 3ᵞ, where γ is greater than 1
Since 3ᵞ is greater than 3, PB is greater than Pₐ
So the final pressure of A is less than that of B

subject: Physics
question: Assertion (A): When 1 g of water freezes at 0° Celsius and 1 atm pressure, the decrease in internal energy is greater than 80 cal (heat of fusion = 80 cal/g). Reason (R): During freezing, water expands, so work is done by the system on the surroundings.
options: A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
explanation:
Water is unusual in that it expands on freezing (which is why ice floats), so the freezing system does positive work on the surroundings, meaning W(by the system) is positive
Heat released during freezing is Q=-80 cal (exothermic)
By the first law, δ U = Q - W(by system) = -80 - (a positive quantity), which is more negative than -80 cal
So the decrease in internal energy exceeds 80 cal, confirming assertion A is true
The reason correctly explains why: the extra work done by the expanding system accounts for the internal energy decrease being larger than the heat released alone

subject: Physics
question: The temperature at which the rms speed of helium molecules equals the rms speed of neon molecules at 400 K is (M(He)=4, M(Ne)=20)
explanation:
v(rms) is ∝ √(T/M)
T(He)/M(He) = T(Ne)/M(Ne)
T(He) = 400 x (⁴⁄₂₀) = 80 K

subject: Physics
question: A person at rest hears a stationary siren, then accelerates at 2 m/s² along a straight line. The distance travelled when the heard frequency drops to 90 percent of the initial value is (speed of sound=340 m/s)
explanation:
For an observer receding from a stationary source, f prime/f = (v-v0)/v
0.90 = (340-v0)/340
v0 = 340(0.10) = 34 m/s
Using v0²=2as: 34² = 2(2)s
1156 = 4s
s = 289 m

subject: Physics
question: An object is placed 20 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. A convex mirror is placed at the focus of the lens on the other side such that the final image coincides with the object. The focal length of the convex mirror is
explanation:
Using the lens formula with u=-20, f=15: 1/v = ¹⁄₁₅-¹⁄₂₀ = ¹⁄₆₀, so v=60 cm
The mirror is placed at the focus, 15 cm from the lens, and the lens image would form at 60 cm from the lens, which is 45 cm from the mirror
For the final image to coincide with the object, this point must be the center of curvature of the mirror, so R=45 cm and the focal length is 22.5 cm

subject: Physics
question: For a prism of angle 4°, the minimum deviation versus refractive index graph is linear. The slope of the graph is
explanation:
For a thin prism, minimum deviation δ = (μ-1)A, which is linear in μ with slope A
Here A=4°, so the slope is 4°

subject: Physics
question: In Youngs double slit experiment, the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is 16:1. The ratio of the intensities of the two slits is
explanation:
(root I1+root I2)/(root I1-root I2) = √(Imax/Imin) = √16 = 4
Let r=√(I1/I2). Then (r+1)/(r-1)=4, giving r+1=4r-4, so r=⁵⁄₃
I1/I2 = r² = ²⁵⁄₉

subject: Physics
question: Two point charges +4×10⁻¹⁹ C and -4×10⁻¹⁹ C are 2 Å apart, forming a dipole in a uniform field of 5×10⁵ V/m. The work done to rotate the dipole from equilibrium by 180° is
explanation:
Dipole moment p = qd = 4×10⁻¹⁹ x 2×10⁻¹⁰ = 8×10⁻²⁹ C.m
Work to rotate a dipole by 180° from stable equilibrium is W=2pE
W = 2 x 8×10⁻²⁹ x 5×10⁵ = 8×10⁻²³ J

subject: Physics
question: A circle of radius r is drawn in a uniform electric field E pointing from top to bottom. E and F are the leftmost and rightmost points on the horizontal diameter, while G and H are the topmost and bottommost points on the vertical diameter. Then
explanation:
E and F lie on a line perpendicular to the field, so they are at the same potential, giving VE=VF
Since the field points downward, potential decreases downward, so G (top, upstream) is at higher potential than H (bottom, downstream), giving VG greater than VH

subject: Physics
question: A 9 V battery is connected to two capacitors C1=3 microF and C2=6 microF in series, and this combination is in parallel with C3=2 microF. The charge on C2 is
explanation:
Series combination: Cs = (3×6)/(3+6) = ¹⁸⁄₉ = 2 microF
This series branch is directly across the 9 V battery
Charge on the series combination = 2 x 9 = 18 microC
Since series capacitors carry the same charge, the charge on C2 is also 18 microC

subject: Physics
question: In a circuit, two 6 Ω resistors are in parallel, and this combination is in series with a third 6 Ω resistor, all connected to a 9 V source. The current drawn from the source is
explanation:
Parallel combination of the two 6 Ω resistors = 3 Ω
Total resistance = 3+6 = 9 Ω
Current = V/R = ⁹⁄₉ = 1 A

subject: Physics
question: In a circuit, two 6 Ω resistors are in parallel, and this combination is in series with a third 6 Ω resistor. Each resistor can dissipate a maximum power of 24 W. The maximum power the whole circuit can take is
explanation:
Parallel combination of two 6 Ω resistors = 3 Ω, in series with the third 6 Ω resistor gives total resistance 9 Ω
The series resistor carries the full current and is the limiting element, restricting current to at most √(²⁴⁄₆)=2 A
Maximum total power = I² x R(total) = 4 x 9 = 36 W

subject: Physics
question: Two long straight parallel wires carrying current in the same direction will
options: exert no force on each other
explanation:
Parallel currents flowing in the same direction attract each other, while currents in opposite directions repel each other
This is a fundamental result from the magnetic force between current-carrying conductors

subject: Physics
question: An electron moves in a circular orbit of radius r with period T. Its magnetic moment is
explanation:
Magnetic moment = current x area
Current I = charge/period = e/T
Area = π r²
Magnetic moment = (e/T)(π r²) = e(π)r²/T

subject: Physics
question: A material has magnetic susceptibility chi = -1 (that is, M=-H exactly). This material is classified as
explanation:
When M=-H exactly, the net magnetic field B=μ₀(H+M)=0 inside the material
This is the behavior of an ideal (perfect) diamagnet, which completely opposes the applied field

subject: Physics
question: In a coil, the current varies from -2 A to +4 A in 3 s, inducing an emf of 0.3 V. The self-inductance of the coil is
explanation:
Change in current = 4-(-2) = 6 A over 3 s
emf = L(δ I/δ t)
0.3 = L(⁶⁄₃) = 2L
L = 0.15 H

subject: Physics
question: For the power dissipated in an LCR series circuit to be one-fourth of the maximum power, the current amplitude should be
explanation:
Power dissipated is ∝ the square of the current amplitude
For power to be one-fourth of the maximum, the current amplitude must be half of the maximum current amplitude

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following statements about electromagnetic waves are correct? (i) They travel as transverse waves (ii) They require a material medium to propagate (iii) They carry momentum (iv) Their electric and magnetic fields oscillate in phase
explanation:
Electromagnetic waves are transverse in nature, so (i) is correct
They do not require a material medium and can travel through vacuum, so (ii) is incorrect
They carry both energy and momentum, so (iii) is correct
The electric and magnetic field components oscillate in phase with each other, so (iv) is correct
Hence the correct statements are (i), (iii), and (iv)

subject: Physics
question: Light of wavelength 2000 Å is incident on a metal surface of work function 5 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is
explanation:
Photon energy = 1240/(wavelength in nm) = ¹²⁴⁰⁄₂₀₀ = 6.2 eV
Maximum kinetic energy = photon energy - work function = 6.2-5 = 1.2 eV

subject: Physics
question: The energy of an electron in a Bohr hydrogen atom is -1.51 eV. The angular momentum of the electron is
explanation:
Energy -1.51 eV corresponds to n=3, since E(n)=-13.6/n² gives -13.⁶⁄₉=-1.51 eV
Angular momentum L = nh/(2 π)
For n=3: L = 3h/(2 π)

subject: Physics
question: The half-life of a radioisotope is 6 minutes. If the number of radioactive nuclei at a given instant is 8×10⁵, the number remaining 3 minutes later would be
explanation:
Since 3 minutes is half of the half-life (6 minutes), N = N0(½)ᵗ/ᵗ
N = 8×10⁵ x (½)³⁄₆ = 8×10⁵ x (½)⁰.⁵ = 8×10⁵/√2

subject: Physics
question: A carrier wave of frequency 3 MHz is used to modulate a message signal of frequency 30 kHz. The frequencies of the side bands produced are
explanation:
Side band frequencies are fc ± fm
fc = 3000 kHz, fm = 30 kHz
Side bands: 3000+30=3030 kHz and 3000-30=2970 kHz

subject: Physics
question: A uniform metre scale balances at the 30 cm mark when a mass of 30 g is suspended at the 5 cm mark. The mass of the scale is
explanation:
Since the scale is uniform, its weight acts at the 50 cm mark
Balancing torques about the 30 cm pivot: 30(30-5) = m(50-30)
30(25) = 20m
750 = 20m
m = 37.5 g

question: A particle has mass 100 g and speed 100 m/s. If the speed is measured with an accuracy of 1 percent, the uncertainty in its position is (h=6.626×10⁻³⁴ J s, π=3.14)
explanation:
Uncertainty in velocity, δ v = 1 percent of 100 = 1 m/s
Using δ x is at least h/(4 π m δ v)
δ x = 6.626×10⁻³⁴/(4 x 3.14 x 0.1 x 1)
= 6.626×10⁻³⁴/1.256
= 5.28×10⁻³⁴ m

subject: Chemistry
question: The work functions of Na, K, Cs, Zn are 2.3, 2.25, 2.14, 4.3 eV respectively. Light of wavelength 400 nm is shone on them. The metals that undergo the photoelectric effect are
explanation:
Photon energy = ¹²⁴⁰⁄₄₀₀ = 3.1 eV
Photoelectric effect occurs only when the photon energy exceeds the work function
3.1 eV exceeds the work functions of Na (2.3), K (2.25), and Cs (2.14), so all three undergo the effect
3.1 eV is less than the work function of Zn (4.3 eV), so Zn does not

subject: Chemistry
question: Among Na, Mg, Al, Si, the element with the highest first ionization enthalpy is
explanation:
Although ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period, there are exceptions due to stable electron configurations
Mg has a higher ionization enthalpy than Al because Mg has a stable filled 3s2 configuration, while Al loses a single 3p electron more easily
However, Si has the highest first ionization enthalpy among this group since it continues the increasing trend after the Al dip and has a half-empty stable arrangement effect building toward P
Comparing the actual values (Na=496, Mg=738, Al=577, Si=786 kJ/mol), Si has the highest

subject: Chemistry
question: The hybridization of the central atom and the shape of ClF₃ are respectively
explanation:
Chlorine in ClF₃ has 3 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, giving a total of 5 electron pairs
This corresponds to sp³d hybridization
With 2 lone pairs occupying equatorial positions of the trigonal bipyramidal arrangement, the resulting molecular shape is T-shaped

subject: Chemistry
question: How many of the following are linear with no lone pairs of electrons on the central atom: CO₂, BeF₂, SO₂, CS₂, NO₂, ZnCl₂?
explanation:
CO₂ is linear with no lone pair on carbon
BeF₂ is linear with no lone pair on beryllium
CS₂ is linear with no lone pair on carbon
ZnCl₂ is linear with no lone pair effect on zinc
SO₂ is bent due to a lone pair on sulfur, and NO₂ is bent due to an unpaired electron effect
So 4 of the molecules qualify: CO₂, BeF₂, CS₂, ZnCl₂

subject: Chemistry
question: At T(K), the rms velocity of an ideal gas is y m/s. At what temperature (in K) does the rms velocity become 5y m/s?
explanation:
v(rms) is ∝ √(T)
(5y/y)² = T2/T1
25 = T2/T
T2 = 25T

subject: Chemistry
question: 6 g of a metal M reacts with chlorine to form 23.75 g of metal chloride. What is the mass of M that reacts with 40 g of oxygen?
explanation:
Mass of chlorine combined = 23.75-6 = 17.75 g
Equivalents of chlorine = 17.⁷⁵⁄₃₅.5 = 0.5
Equivalent weight of M = ⁶⁄₀.5 = 12
Equivalents of oxygen in 40 g = ⁴⁰⁄₈ = 5 (equivalent weight of oxygen is 8)
Mass of M = 5 x 12 = 60 g

subject: Chemistry
question: Combustion of ethylene gives CO₂(g) and H₂O(l). If the enthalpies of formation of C₂H₄(g), CO₂(g), H₂O(l) are -a, -b, -c kJ/mol respectively, the enthalpy of combustion of C₂H₄(g) is
explanation:
The combustion reaction is C₂H₄(g)+3O2(g) to 2CO₂(g)+2H₂O(l)
Enthalpy of combustion = sum of enthalpies of formation of products minus that of reactants
= [2(-b)+2(-c)] - [(-a)+0]
= -2b-2c+a
= a-2b-2c

subject: Chemistry
question: Identify the correct statements: I. Specific heat capacity is an intensive property II. A coffee-cup calorimeter measures heat change at constant pressure III. The SI unit of heat capacity is J/K
explanation:
Specific heat capacity, being defined per unit mass, does not depend on the amount of substance, so it is intensive, making I correct
A coffee-cup calorimeter is open to the atmosphere and operates at constant pressure, making II correct
The correct SI unit for heat capacity is joule per kelvin (J/K), making III correct
So all three statements are correct

subject: Chemistry
question: Consider A(g)+B(g) reversible C(g)+D(g). In a 2 L closed flask, 3 moles of A and 2 moles of B were heated. At equilibrium, the concentration of D is twice that of B. What is Kc?
explanation:
Let x moles react. At equilibrium: A=3-x, B=2-x, C=x, D=x
Given D=2B: x=2(2-x), so x=⁴⁄₃
Concentrations (dividing by 2 L): A=(⁵⁄₃)/2=⅚, B=(⅔)/2=⅓, C=(⁴⁄₃)/2=⅔, D=⅔
Kc = (C)(D)/[(A)(B)] = (⅔ x ⅔)/(⅚ x ⅓) = (⁴⁄₉)/(⁵⁄₁₈) = ⁷²⁄₄₅ = 1.6

subject: Chemistry
question: The dissociation constants of H2A are Kₐ₁=4×10⁻³ and Kₐ₂=4×10⁻⁷. At equilibrium, [A2-]=[H2A]. The approximate concentration of H⁺ at equilibrium is
explanation:
Multiplying the equilibrium expressions for Kₐ₁ and Kₐ₂ eliminates the intermediate ion: Kₐ₁ x Kₐ₂ = [H⁺]² [A2-]/[H2A]
Since [A2-]=[H2A], this ratio is 1, so [H⁺]² = Kₐ₁ x Kₐ₂ = 16×10⁻¹⁰
[H⁺] = 4×10⁻⁵

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following metals commonly forms an interstitial hydride that retains its original crystal lattice: Pd, Na, Ca, Fe?
explanation: Palladium is the classic example of a metal that absorbs large volumes of hydrogen gas to form an interstitial hydride, PdHx, without significantly disrupting its original face-centered cubic lattice

subject: Chemistry
question: When sodium nitrate and silver nitrate are heated separately, which observation is common to both?
options: Oxygen gas is evolved in both cases
Brown NO₂ fumes are evolved in both cases
No gas is evolved in either case
explanation:
Sodium nitrate, like most alkali metal nitrates (except lithium), decomposes on heating to give sodium nitrite and oxygen gas
Silver nitrate decomposes on heating to give metallic silver, brown NO₂ fumes, and oxygen gas
While NO₂ fumes are unique to silver nitrate, the evolution of oxygen gas is common to both decompositions

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Diborane is used as a rocket fuel component
Boron nitride exists in a graphite-like layered structure
Boric acid is a strong acid
The borax bead test is used to identify colored metal ions
explanation:
The borax bead test, the use of diborane in rocket propulsion, and the graphite-like layered structure of boron nitride are all correct facts
However, boric acid is actually a weak monobasic Lewis acid, not a strong acid, since it accepts a hydroxide ion rather than directly donating a proton
So the statement calling boric acid a strong acid is incorrect

subject: Chemistry
question: The number of amphoteric oxides among Al₂O₃, ZnO, MgO, BeO, CaO, Na₂O is
explanation:
Al₂O₃, ZnO, and BeO are amphoteric oxides, reacting with both acids and bases
MgO, CaO, and Na₂O are basic oxides
So the number of amphoteric oxides is 3

subject: Chemistry
question: The catalytic cycle of ozone depletion by chlorine radicals (Cl + O3 to ClO + O₂) is temporarily terminated when chlorine is tied up in which reservoir species?
explanation:
Chlorine radicals can be temporarily removed from the ozone-destroying catalytic cycle by combining with methane or nitrogen dioxide to form relatively stable reservoir species such as hydrogen chloride (HCl) and chlorine nitrate (ClONO₂)
These reservoir species can later release active chlorine again under the right conditions

subject: Chemistry
question: A mixture of aniline and water, which are immiscible and where aniline decomposes near its normal boiling point, is best separated by
explanation:
Steam distillation allows a substance to distill at a temperature below its normal boiling point by using the combined vapor pressure of the substance and steam
This is ideal for aniline, which would decompose if heated to its actual boiling point under simple distillation

subject: Chemistry
question: 1-Butene reacts with water under acid catalysis to give X (Markovnikov addition). Isopentane (2-methylbutane) is oxidized at its tertiary carbon to give Y. X and Y respectively are
explanation:
Markovnikov addition of water to 1-butene places the hydroxyl group on the more substituted carbon, giving butan-2-ol as X
Oxidation at the tertiary carbon (C2) of isopentane gives the tertiary alcohol 2-methylbutan-2-ol as Y

subject: Chemistry
question: The IUPAC name of CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₂-OH is
explanation:
Numbering the four-carbon chain to give the hydroxyl group the lowest locant, the OH is on C1, and the methyl branch is on C3
This gives the name 3-methylbutan-1-ol

subject: Chemistry
question: Atoms of element B form a ccp (fcc) lattice, and atoms of element A occupy half of the octahedral voids. The formula of the compound formed is
explanation:
In a ccp lattice, the effective number of atoms per unit cell is 4, and the number of octahedral voids equals the number of atoms, that is 4
A occupies half of these voids: (½) x 4 = 2 atoms of A
Ratio of A to B = 2:4 = 1:2
So the formula is AB2

subject: Chemistry
question: 1.5 g of a non-electrolytic, non-volatile solute is dissolved in 25 g of water. The freezing point of the solution is found to be -0.9° Celsius. The molar mass of the solute is (Kf of water = 1.86 K kg/mol)
explanation:
Depression in freezing point = 0-(-0.9) = 0.9° Celsius
molality = 0.⁹⁄₁.86 = 0.4839 mol/kg
Moles of solute = 0.4839 x 0.025 = 0.0121 mol
Molar mass = 1.⁵⁄₀.0121 = 124 g/mol

subject: Chemistry
question: For the cell reaction Zn(s)+Cu₂⁺(aq) to Zn₂⁺(aq)+Cu(s), given E(Zn₂⁺/Zn)=-0.76 V, E(Cu₂⁺/Cu)=+0.34 V, and F=96500 C/mol, the standard Gibbs free energy change (in kJ/mol) is
explanation:
E(cell) = E(cathode) - E(anode) = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V
Number of electrons transferred, n=2
δ G = -nFE(cell) = -2 x 96500 x 1.10 = -212300 J = -212.3 kJ

subject: Chemistry
question: Molten NaCl is electrolyzed. The mass of sodium produced at the cathode when 4825 amperes is passed for 500 seconds is (F=96500 C/mol, atomic mass of Na=23)
explanation:
Charge passed, Q = It = 4825 x 500 = 2412500 C
Equivalents deposited = Q/F = ²⁴¹²⁵⁰⁰⁄₉₆₅₀₀ = 25
Since Na⁺ +e- to Na, the equivalent weight equals the atomic mass, 23
Mass deposited = 25 x 23 = 575 g

subject: Chemistry
question: A reaction rate constant at 400 K is ten × that at 300 K. Using R=2 cal/K mol and log10=1, the activation energy is approximately
explanation:
Using the Arrhenius equation: 2.303 log(k2/k1) = (Ea/R)(1/T1 - 1/T2)
2.303(1) = (Ea/2)(¹⁄₃₀₀ - ¹⁄₄₀₀)
2.303 = (Ea/2)(¹⁰⁰⁄₁₂₀₀₀₀)
2.303 = Ea/2400
Ea = 2.303 x 2400 = 5527 cal/mol, which is about 5.5 kcal/mol

subject: Chemistry
question: Which ion is most effective for coagulating a negatively charged As₂S₃ sol?
explanation:
As₂S₃ forms a negatively charged sol, so it requires a cation for coagulation
By the Hardy-Schulze rule, a cation with higher charge is more effective
Among the given ions, Al₃⁺ has the highest charge and is therefore the most effective coagulant

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following are true for physisorption but not for chemisorption? I. It is reversible in nature II. It can form multilayers III. It shows high specificity
explanation:
Physisorption is reversible because it involves only weak van der Waals forces, so I is a property of physisorption but not chemisorption (which is largely irreversible)
Physisorption can occur in multiple layers since the weak forces do not restrict adsorption to a single layer, so II is also unique to physisorption
High specificity is a feature of chemisorption, not physisorption, so III is incorrect
Hence statements I and II are correct

subject: Chemistry
question: Which method is used to refine germanium and silicon to ultra-high purity for semiconductor use?
explanation: Zone refining exploits the difference in solubility of impurities in the molten and solid states of a substance, and is the standard method used to obtain ultra-pure germanium and silicon for semiconductor applications

subject: Chemistry
question: What oxoacid of phosphorus is formed when white phosphorus reacts with hot concentrated NaOH solution (on acidification of the resulting salt)?
explanation:
White phosphorus reacts with hot concentrated NaOH in a disproportionation reaction to give phosphine (PH₃) and sodium hypophosphite (NaH₂PO₂)
Acidifying the sodium hypophosphite gives hypophosphorous acid, H₃PO₂

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the structures of CO₂ and SO₂?
options: Both CO₂ and SO₂ are bent
Both have identical hybridization at the central atom
CO₂ is linear while SO₂ is bent
Both CO₂ and SO₂ are linear
explanation:
CO₂ has a linear shape with sp hybridization at carbon and no lone pairs
SO₂ has a bent shape with sp² hybridization at sulfur due to one lone pair on the central atom
So the two molecules differ in both shape and hybridization, and it is correct that CO₂ is linear while SO₂ is bent

subject: Chemistry
question: Among Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, the element with the lowest first ionization enthalpy has a spin-only magnetic moment (in BM) in its +2 oxidation state of
explanation:
Scandium has the lowest first ionization enthalpy among these elements, being the leftmost element of the group
Sc₂⁺ has the electron configuration [Ar]3d1, with one unpaired electron
Spin-only magnetic moment = √[n(n+2)] = √(1×3) = √3 = 1.73 BM

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following is an ambidentate ligand?
explanation:
An ambidentate ligand can coordinate to a metal ion through either of two different donor atoms
The thiocyanate ion, SCN⁻, can bind through either the sulfur atom or the nitrogen atom, making it a classic example of an ambidentate ligand

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following polymers does NOT contain an amide (-CONH-) linkage in its structure?
explanation:
Nylon 6,6, Nylon 6, and Kevlar are all polyamides, containing repeated amide linkages in their backbone
Terylene (Dacron), on the other hand, is a polyester formed from ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid, containing ester linkages rather than amide linkages

subject: Chemistry
question: Match the amino acids Glycine, Valine, Aspartic acid, Lysine with their R groups: I. -H II. -CH(CH₃)₂ III. -CH₂COOH IV. -(CH₂)₄NH₂
explanation:
Glycine has the simplest side chain, a single hydrogen atom, matching I
Valine has the isopropyl side chain -CH(CH₃)₂, matching II
Aspartic acid has the acidic side chain -CH₂COOH, matching III
Lysine has the basic side chain -(CH₂)₄NH₂, matching IV
So the correct match is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV, taking A,B,C,D as Glycine, Valine, Aspartic acid, Lysine respectively

subject: Chemistry
question: Consider two statements: I. Penicillin is a narrow spectrum antibiotic II. Sulfonamides act as competitive inhibitors of the enzyme that uses PABA (para-aminobenzoic acid). The correct option is
options: Statement I is not correct but II is correct
Both statements I and II are correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Statement I is correct but II is not correct
explanation:
Penicillin is indeed classified as a narrow spectrum antibiotic, effective mainly against certain types of bacteria, so statement I is correct
Sulfonamide drugs act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme that normally uses para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) in bacterial folic acid synthesis, so statement II is also correct

subject: Chemistry
question: An organic compound C₄H₉Cl(A) reacts with alcoholic KOH predominantly via the E2 mechanism, and with aqueous KOH mainly via SN₁ with racemization. The type of halide A is
explanation:
A tertiary alkyl halide readily undergoes E2 elimination with a strong base like alcoholic KOH, since elimination is favored over substitution due to steric hindrance at the tertiary carbon
With a weaker nucleophile like aqueous KOH, tertiary halides favor the SN₁ pathway, which proceeds through a planar carbocation intermediate leading to racemization
So A must be a tertiary halide

subject: Chemistry
question: But-2-yne reacts with 2 moles of HBr. The major product formed (both additions following Markovnikov orientation) is
explanation:
But-2-yne (CH₃-C-triple bond-C-CH₃) is a symmetric internal alkyne
The first addition of HBr gives an intermediate bromoalkene, and the second addition of HBr (following Markovnikov orientation, both bromine atoms adding to the same carbon due to the stability of the resulting carbocation) gives 2,2-dibromobutane as the major product

subject: Chemistry
question: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with CuBr/HBr (Sandmeyer reaction) to give
explanation:
The Sandmeyer reaction replaces the diazonium group with a halogen using a copper(I) halide catalyst
Reacting benzenediazonium chloride with CuBr/HBr replaces the diazonium group with bromine, giving bromobenzene

subject: Chemistry
question: The ratio of σ electrons to π electrons in acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is
explanation:
Acetic acid has 7 σ bonds: 3 C-H bonds in the methyl group, 1 C-C bond, 1 C=O σ bond, 1 C-O bond, and 1 O-H bond, giving 14 σ electrons
It has 1 π bond (the C=O π bond), giving 2 π electrons
Ratio of σ electrons to π electrons = 14:2 = 7:1

subject: Chemistry
question: Formaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH to give methanol and sodium formate. If methanol and formic acid (obtained by acidifying sodium formate) undergo acid-catalyzed esterification, the product is
explanation:
The Cannizzaro reaction of formaldehyde with concentrated NaOH produces equal amounts of methanol and sodium formate
Acidifying sodium formate gives formic acid, which then undergoes Fischer esterification with methanol under acid catalysis to give methyl formate

subject: Chemistry
question: N,N-Diethylbenzenesulphonamide is formed by the reaction between the Hinsberg reagent and
explanation:
N,N-Diethylbenzenesulphonamide has no N-H bond because both hydrogen atoms on nitrogen have been replaced by ethyl groups
This fully N,N-disubstituted product forms specifically from the reaction of the Hinsberg reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) with a secondary amine, such as diethylamine
